content:
maya: quick heads up — production batcher hit a cluster of OOMs this morning when a few long requests pushed batch size from 8 -> 22.
ben: ugh. which path? continuous batching or the old fixed window?
maya: continuous batching. repro in staging with synthetic workload: increasing seq-length distribution causes allocator workspace to grow, then we keep padding for all earlier items in the batch. pad waste skyrockets.
ari: can you paste the perf trace?
maya: pasted below (trimmed):
```
[profile] batch_growth: start_size=8 -> end_size=22
[mem] workspace_reserved=14.2GB workspace_used=9.1GB pad_waste=4.7GB
[kv] persistent_kv=2.1GB per_seq_kv_overhead=24KB
[alloc] peak_frag=1.9GB free_slabs=0.4GB OOM_at=alloc_workspace(1.2GB)
```
maya: note the OOM fires during kernel selection step when we switch to a long-seq kernel and allocate a larger workspace for per-layer fused ops.
ben: hmm that matches the allocator metrics i've seen: we eagerly grow workspace when max_seq changes, but we don't trim between micro-batches. that + KV retention is lethal.
sam: perf-ci uploaded an artifact for the run: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1782104321/artifact (logs + pprof)
perf-ci: artifact uploaded: flamegraph.svg, heap_snapshot.pb
ari: two contributing things: (1) padding waste due to continuous batching (older items carrying new max_seq pad) (2) long-lived KV reservations for streams that are idle but pinned by routing
ben: thoughts on mitigation: a) lazy_workspace_resize (only grow on demand per-layer, reclaim after layer close), b) ephemeral buffer pool for kernel temporaries that can be returned immediately, c) early KV eviction policy for unaccessed streams > Xs, and d) tighter per-seq accounting to charge padding to request owner for rollout metrics.
maya: did quick PoC for lazy resize on cpu: reduced peak by ~22% on the synthetic test, no correctness changes.
ben: can you share the PoC diff or pseudocode? need to check concurrency impacts.
maya: gist of it:
```
// on forward start for layer L
if (required_workspace > current_workspace) {
  // allocate incremental slab only, not entire worst-case slab
  allocate_incremental(required_workspace - current_workspace);
}
... run kernels ...
// after layer finish
if (current_workspace > soft_limit) {
  trim_to(soft_limit); // return slabs to pool asynchronously
}
```
sam: re: KV: we should avoid hard evict during request processing; instead mark candidates and evict between microbatch rounds. also we could memory-account KV at per-shard granularity when deciding workspace growth.
ari: agree. plus kernel selection should have a cheap estimate of incremental workspace cost. current kernel picker returns only throughput estimate, no mem delta.
ben: okay action items: 1) ada: add mem_delta to kernel_picker API (small change) 2) maya: open a branch for lazy_workspace_resize with unit tests + stress harness 3) ari: propose KV idle eviction TTL and passive marking 4) sam: add a perf CI job that runs seq-growth synthetic nightly and captures heap/pprof
maya: i'll open PR for (2) today, include the microbenchmark and the pprof from the PoC.
ben: i'll spec the kernel_picker change — should be backwards compatible: add optional mem_delta field that the allocator can query before commit.
ari: for short-term: increase guard threshold on dedicated hosts so we don't transitively OOM; long-term we land lazy-resize + KV eviction.
sam: also adding alert rule: if pad_waste / workspace_reserved > 0.25 for > 2min, page eng-runtime oncall.
maya: small note: padding waste metrics currently aggregate per-host. would be nice to break out by route/model so product can detect bad prompts.
ben: good call. add model_id tag to mem telemetry.
maya: thanks all — i'll drop the PR link here and tag @ben for review. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job: batcher-lazy-resize-poctest -> staging (run in 10m)
perf-ci: nightly synthetic seq-growth job added to pipeline: /pipelines/seq-growth
ben: once PR lands, let's run the canary with perf profiling enabled and compare flamegraphs before/after. aim for <10% reg on p99 latency and >15% drop in peak memory.
maya: will do. last note: watch out for allocator fragmentation when trimming aggressively — we need to prefer returning contiguous slabs or merging small free blocks before trim.
ari: noted. fragmentation check added to allocator QA checklist.
maya: end.
